name: Matar
description: A naked-eye star 65.7 parsecs away, 24.5 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: radius 24.51 +1.21/-1.11 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.471 +/- 0.027 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: mass 3.51 +/- 0.13 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: effective temperature 4970 +/- 65 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 215182: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 15.22 +/- 0.71 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 66 parsecs away whose disc the NPOI measured: 24.5 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 3.471 milliarcseconds, which gives 24.51 solar radii and 4,970 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 215182: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1887953690728237568 (quality A), from 2004A&A...424..727P; Gaia DR3 measures none
